criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Launch, SSO elements, manoeuvre, ground station accesses via STK and 5-yr EOL with drag sail covered with screenshots and calculations, though some technical slips remain.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings and readable writing, but figures lack numbers/titles, tables poorly formatted, Wikipedia used despite ban, referencing inconsistent.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved

technical_issues.issue: RAAN 27.33 deg claimed to indicate launch facility location; RAAN is orbit plane orientation, not site, and will not equal site longitude.
Circular orbit described with Argument of Latitude as static element; u varies rapidly and LTAN/local time not specified for SSO.
Baseline Vega E in 2025 was unflown/developmental; reliance on future SSMS replication adds schedule risk, acknowledged but weakly mitigated.
Wikipedia cited for launch manifest despite explicit ban; reference list is bare URLs without proper citation style.

overall: Good reef-monitoring SSO concept with credible STK support, but weakened by orbit detail errors, unproven launcher baseline and presentation/referencing flaws.

feedback.summary: You produced a good reef-monitoring SSO concept with credible STK work. Your Introduction and mission design are strong, but orbit detail errors, an unproven Vega E baseline, a generic Conclusion and referencing flaws limit you. Fixing these will lift you to the top of each rubric band.
next_steps: In Mission Design - Orbit, correct RAAN 27.33 deg and Argument of Latitude: explain RAAN/LTAN properly and give LTAN/local time for your 600km SSO.
Strengthen your Vega E from Guiana baseline with flight status and a backup launcher/SSMS option to address schedule risk you noted.
In Conclusion and throughout, add numbered figure titles, clean table formatting, and replace bare URLs/Wikipedia with proper in-text citations and reference list.

criteria.C1: You did well in Introduction stating your Earth observation mission for coral reef and ocean monitoring, justifying one satellite for simplicity, and naming users like CSIRO and BOM with literature refs. To reach the top of Accomplished, make your operator role explicit.
criteria.C2: You did well in Mission Design - Launch/Orbit and Ground Control & Communications covering Vega E from Guiana, 600km 97.7924 deg SSO, manoeuvres, Mean Duration accesses in Image 4, and 5-yr drag-sail EOL with STK screenshots. For higher Accomplished, fix RAAN-site confusion, static Argument of Latitude, missing LTAN, and mitigate Vega E risk.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion summarises launch, orbit, ground station and benefit starting 'fully described satellite configuration...'. For Accomplished, move beyond generic summary to detailed conclusions directly synthesised from your STK results, calculations and trade-offs.
criteria.C4: Your Executive Summary 'This report outlines...' and headings make the report readable. For Accomplished, give all figures numbers/titles, format tables consistently, and fix Bibliography 'https://en.wikipedia.org...' bare URLs and banned Wikipedia use with proper citations.
